newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds were heading to a higher close, but off a new intra-day record hit briefly on Tuesday afternoon, dealers said.
The tone of the market was positive in anticipation of good October inflation data -- due on Thursday -- but a weaker dollar put a cap on the bulls in the peripheral markets, dealers said.
"In these last months it has been normal to see long positions before the Cpi," said Emilio Sainz of Natwest.
The new intra-day high in the December contract was set at 109.55, while the previous on November 8 was at 109.53, where chartists put strong resistance.
Other dealers were surprised by bonos strength.

"Yesterday the Ecofin didn't reach any agreement over the stability pact and Germany doesn't like a broad start for Europe's single currency," Alessandro Ceccaroni, at UBS in London, said. "EMU perspectives are different now."
The 10-year spread over German Bunds declined a little to end at 159 basis points from 163 bps. Its record low was 152.
Dealers added the yield curve flattened today.
"People are more interested in buying longer term before the Cpi," said Sainz. "Three- and five- year bonds lost ground to the 10-year bonds".
